title: Claude Ship: 1 Policy File Lets AI Approve Routine PRs
description:
Claude Ship explained in 60 seconds: AI agents that take your GitHub PRs through review, fixes and an approval decision; PR Steward tries to fix failing checks, merge conflicts and review comments, and Claude Approvals can approve routine PRs on its own when your team's policy file allows it.
In beta since November 23, 2026, on Claude Team and Enterprise plans for GitHub repositories (Code Review is generally available). Our example: 1 routine pull request stopped you 4 times; now 0, if PR Steward's fixes work and your policy file lets Claude approve.

Read Anthropic's own post first: https://claude.com/resources/articles/introducing-claude-ship

Chapters
0:00 Our example: 4 stops, 1 PR
0:18 PR Steward tries, policy decides
0:29 Routine vs risky, Anthropic's proof
0:41 What we learned (our example)

The story: one counted example. One routine pull request, a small docs fix, shown as a small boat in a harbour. In our example it has 1 failing check, 1 merge conflict and 1 review comment, and then 1 approval to chase: 4 times you stop your next task. In our example, before, an AI review only left comments and you did the rest yourself, so 1 pull request stopped you 4 times. Now, in beta, PR Steward works on the check, the conflict and the comment while you keep coding, and Claude Approvals can approve this kind of routine change if your team's policy allows: 0 stops in our example, if the fixes work and your policy allows.

How it works, per Anthropic: Claude Ship is made up of Code Review (generally available) and two agents in beta, PR Steward and Claude Approvals. PR Steward works on failing CI checks, merge conflicts and review feedback: it pushes commits to address review feedback and attempts to fix failing checks and resolve merge conflicts (a failing check only when the cause is in code the pull request touches). After every push it comments with what it changed and how to undo it, and it is designed not to approve or merge pull requests. Claude Approvals applies an approval policy that your team writes as a file in the repository (.claude/approvals.yml): Claude can approve routine changes on its own if the policy allows it, or the policy can require deeper human sign-off for certain scenarios. Anthropic's docs example: billing code can need two people, with more people on risky changes and fewer on routine ones. The check blocks a merge only where you make it a required check in GitHub.

Before you turn it on: Claude Ship is available on Claude Team and Enterprise plans for repositories on GitHub; it is not available to organizations with Zero Data Retention, the HIPAA configuration or customer-managed encryption keys. Usage is billed on tokens, so turning it on can add to an organization's costs. Anthropic recommends enabling it first in observe-only mode to build confidence. Claude Ship uses AI and may miss bugs, security vulnerabilities or other issues.

The number: on Anthropic's own Claude Code team, where Claude's review is one layer of a broader process, merged PRs more than doubled from June to September. That is Anthropic's number for its own team, given where its post describes Code Review; it is not a promise for your team.
